value.description: Felix rides through the forest with Sable and explains his reasoning about Wren, the map, and the thieves.
evidence: Felix and Sable ride a dirt road through tall pines, moving at pace.

FELIX
If Wren has the map he will move it through the eastern fences.

FELIX
No. I had moved it. Too late, as it turns out.

value.description: Sable rides beside Felix and questions him about Wren, the map description, and where the thieves searched.
evidence: Felix and Sable ride a dirt road through tall pines, moving at pace.
Sable rides beside Felix, her long dark brown hair pulled back under a riding hood.

SABLE
How can you be certain?

value.description: Wren is the influential nobleman Felix suspects would move the map through the eastern fences.
evidence: If Wren has the map he will move it through the eastern fences.
Because of who he is. A nobleman with reach across three provinces.

surface_forms: a map of the Northern Reaches
value.description: The sought-after map is the central object of the discussion, described as a version of the Northern Reaches map and moved by Felix.
evidence: If Wren has the map he will move it through the eastern fences.
They described a map of the Northern Reaches drawn in red ink on reinforced parchment.
No. I had moved it.

value.description: The eastern fences are the route Felix says Wren would use to move the map.
evidence: he will move it through the eastern fences.

value.description: The three provinces are the extent of Wren's political reach as described by Felix.
evidence: A nobleman with reach across three provinces.

value.description: The thief is the person whose incorrect description of the map prompts Felix's explanation.
evidence: What about the description the thief gave? You said it was wrong.

value.description: The Northern Reaches are the region depicted on the map Felix discusses.
evidence: They described a map of the Northern Reaches drawn in red ink on reinforced parchment.

value.description: Holt is the person Felix cites as the source for how the fence described the map.
evidence: That is how Holt said the fence described it.

value.description: The fence is the intermediary whose description of the map Holt reportedly relayed.
evidence: That is how Holt said the fence described it.

value.description: The chest is the container Sable references when asking where the thieves found the map.
evidence: And the chest -- where they found it.

value.description: The window alcove is the hiding place area where Felix kept the map in a wooden box on a shelf.
evidence: The window alcove?
the wooden box I kept on the alcove shelf.

value.description: The thieves are the people Felix says had seen the map earlier and returned expecting it to still be in its old hiding place.
evidence: They must have seen it earlier in the wooden box I kept on the alcove shelf.
They assumed it was still there when they came back for it.

value.description: The wooden box is the container in which Felix previously kept the map on the alcove shelf.
evidence: the wooden box I kept on the alcove shelf.
